bull.b: The debt-free balance sheet and reported liquidity provide financial flexibility while the platform is still being commercialized. Management estimates immediately available funds cover roughly 18 months and total liquidity roughly three years, assuming no incremental revenue.

The sharp sequential reduction in operating expenses and losses shows management can materially adjust the cost base. Sustaining this discipline would extend liquidity, reduce the revenue scale needed for breakeven, and improve operating leverage as tokenized-gold adoption develops.

Completed custody, attestation, brokerage and liquidity relationships address important access requirements for institutional users. This infrastructure can support broader distribution of GLDY and future products, giving the company a more credible foundation for scaling beyond early adopters.

bear.b: Revenue remains far too small to absorb the company’s cost structure, while very large losses indicate that commercial validation has not yet translated into earnings power. Until revenue scales substantially, profitability and margin sustainability remain highly uncertain.

Negative operating and free cash flow show the business is not yet self-funding and continues to depend on outside funding or existing liquidity. Even with lower expected burn, ongoing cash consumption can constrain investment and shorten the runway if adoption takes longer.

The Nasdaq deficiency creates an ongoing corporate and trading-venue risk that management must resolve within the stated grace period. Failure to regain compliance could lead to further delisting proceedings, increasing operational uncertainty and potentially complicating access to public capital.
